result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.line_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the line graph of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11491-L11657){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.line_graph(create_using_directed=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The line graph `L(G)` of a graph `G` transforms edges into nodes: each edge in `G` becomes a node in `L(G)`, and two nodes in `L(G)` are connected if and only if their corresponding edges in `G` share an endpoint. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [create_using_directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the resulting line graph should be directed. - If `None` (default): inherits directedness from source graph - If `True`: creates a directed line graph - If `False`: creates an undirected line graph For directed graphs, edge `(u,v)` connects to edge `(v,w)` if they share the intermediate node `v` (i.e., head of first = tail of second). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph representing the line graph. Each node in the line graph corresponds to an edge in the original graph, with attributes: - `source`: source node label of the original edge - `target`: target node label of the original edge - `edge_id`: ID of the original edge - `weight`: weight of the original edge (if weighted) ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Definition**: For a graph `G = (V, E)`, the line graph `L(G) = (E, E')`, where nodes in `L(G)` are edges of `G`, and edges in `L(G)` connect adjacent edges in `G`. **Adjacency Rules**: - **Undirected graphs**: edges are adjacent if they share any vertex; edge `{a, b}` is adjacent to edge `{b, c}` because they share node `b` - **Directed graphs**: edge `(u, v)` is adjacent to edge `(v, w)` only; the head of the first edge must equal the tail of the second **Properties**: - `|V(L(G))| = |E(G)|` (line graph has as many nodes as `G` has edges) - For undirected `G`: `|E(L(G))| = (1/2) * Σ deg(v)² - |E(G)|` - The line graph of a complete graph `Kₙ` is a triangular graph - The line graph of a cycle is another cycle of the same length **Use Cases**: - edge clustering: cluster edges by treating them as nodes - network flow analysis: study edge relationships - social networks: analyze "edge communities" - transportation: model transfer points between routes - dual representations: some graph problems are easier on L(G) ## Examples {.doc-examples} Line graph of a simple path: ::: {#29e51b9c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create path: A -- B -- C g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("B", "C") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 2 (one per edge) lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#5b1c6a18 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 1 (edges A-B and B-C share B) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Line graph of a triangle: ::: {#09ba9cef .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Triangle: A -- B -- C -- A g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("B", "C") g.add_edge("C", "A") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 3 lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#2b586976 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 3 (also a triangle) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Line graph of a directed graph: ::: {#48532a7b .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Chain: A -> B -> C g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("B", "C") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 2 lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#27476aa2 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 1 (A->B connects to B->C) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Accessing original edge information: ::: {#868bc9e4 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="X") g.add_node(label="Y") g.add_node(label="Z") g.add_edge("X", "Y", weight=2.0) g.add_edge("Y", "Z", weight=3.0) lg = g.line_graph() [lg.get_node(nid).attributes for nid in lg.get_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` [{'original_edge_id': 2, 'original_source': 2, 'original_target': 3, 'original_weight': 3.0}, {'original_edge_id': 1, 'original_source': 1, 'original_target': 2, 'original_weight': 2.0}] ``` ::: ::: Line graph of a star graph: ::: {#21e9a3b0 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Star with center C g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="C") for i in range(4): g.add_node(label=f"L{i}") g.add_edge("C", f"L{i}") lg = g.line_graph() # Returns 4 (one per spoke) lg.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3a935824 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 6 (all spokes share center - line graph of a star is a complete graph!) lg.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` 6 ``` ::: :::
